body:
## Blocks

#40.

Seven findings from the full-tree review at `b3190d2` that are each too small
for a ticket of their own. Every one was reproduced before filing. They are
independent: a fix may take them in any order, and dropping one with a recorded
reason is a legitimate answer for several.

This ticket has the shape #66 had for the same review's earlier round.

---

### 1. `R/nest_with_margins.R:83` names a different dplyr verb than the section it points at

The `@return` and the *Result class and attributes* section render on the same
help page and contradict each other.

`R/nest_with_margins.R:83`:

> For a local input, an ungrouped data frame with one list column, whose class
> and attributes follow [dplyr::summarize()]; see *Result class and attributes*.

`R/summarize_with_margins.R:207`, which owns that section:

> [summarize_with_margins()] those of [dplyr::summarize()], and
> [expand_with_margins()] and **the nesting verbs** those of [dplyr::mutate()]
> combined with [dplyr::union_all()].

`R/expand_with_margins.R:37` states its own return against the section
correctly, which is what makes this a drifted copy rather than an exception.
`design/architecture.md`'s module chapter agrees with the section. No input was
found on which the two rules give different answers, so this is an
inconsistency on a shipped page rather than a wrong result — but a reader
following the `@return` has the wrong rule for a data-frame subclass, where
`summarize()` and `mutate()` reconstruct differently.

### 2. `.Rbuildignore` has no `^\.git$`, so a tarball built in a worktree ships `.git`

`R CMD build` strips `.git` only when it is a *directory*. In a git worktree —
the layout this repository works in daily, under `.claude/worktrees/` — `.git`
is a regular file holding `gitdir:`, and R's build-time exclusions do not match
it. The tarball then carries it and `R CMD check --as-cran` raises a second
NOTE on top of the New-submission one:

```
* checking for hidden files and directories ... NOTE
Found the following hidden files and directories:
  .git
```

Measured both ways against this tree: without the entry the tarball holds
`marginplyr/.git`; with `^\.git$` appended it holds none. PR #490 recorded the
trap in its body and worked around it by exporting first; nothing in the tree
prevents the next person from hitting it. One line fixes it.

### 3. `vignettes/get_started.qmd:61` guards on `knitr`, which `AGENTS.md` says can never be absent

```r
has_tabsets <- marginplyr_suggest_available("knitr") &&
  marginplyr_suggest_available("quartabs")
```

`AGENTS.md` *Chunks that must fail* states the fact directly, as its reason the
hook `source()` needs no guard: "quarto imports rmarkdown, which imports knitr
— the `DBI = FALSE` case from *Dependency metadata*, so a guard on knitr in a
vignette would never fire." Verified by the check that rule prescribes:
`packageDescription("quarto")$Imports` names `rmarkdown`;
`packageDescription("rmarkdown")$Imports` names `knitr (>= 1.50)`. The left
conjunct is dead; `quartabs` is what decides. This is the only such site.

### 4. `design/adr/0010-*.md` uses three terms `CONTEXT.md` lists under `_Avoid_`

`CONTEXT.md`'s **Grand total set** entry ends `_Avoid_: Root set, root row,
total row, margin row`, and `design/agents/domain.md` says "Do not drift to
synonyms that the glossary explicitly avoids." The ADR uses:

- `:19` "The **root row** has a Parent share of `1`."
- `:68` "**root grand-total row** only"
- `:212` "every **non-root row**"

The same file already writes the canonical term at `:473`, so two spellings sit
in one document. #486's House-term sweep was about capitalization and would not
have caught a synonym.

Whether an ADR's *Decision* text is in scope for a vocabulary edit is the one
judgement here: `design/architecture.md` *Repository placement* amends an ADR
only when its decision changed observably. Recording "out of scope, and here is
why" closes this item.

### 5. `R/grouping-adapter-native.R:51` passes an argument the body never reads

```r
flag_quos <- Map(
  function(var, name) {
    rlang::new_quosure(grouping_sql_expr(var, con), env = rlang::empty_env())
  },
  labelled_dimensions,
  flag_names
)
names(flag_quos) <- flag_names
```

`name` appears nowhere in the body, and the names `Map()` would set are
overwritten on the next line. `lapply(labelled_dimensions, ...)` says on its
face that the flag name plays no part in building the quosure.

This is not only a smell: #23's Implementation Decisions ask for exactly it —
"Fragile local-state patterns are removed: ... remove unused arguments and
no-op expressions".

### 6. Two selection readings are each written out more than once

**The summary selection proxy**, `dplyr::select(proxy, dplyr::all_of(setdiff(data_vars, unique(group_vars))))`,
is built from scratch at three sites: `R/summary-selections.R:447` and `:545`,
and `R/summarize_with_margins.R:934`. `group_vars` is `c(plan$by, plan$dimensions)`
at every one, so all three are the same value, computed four times per
`summarize_with_margins()` call.

`design/architecture.md` *Module responsibilities* gives `R/summary-selections.R`
ownership of "resolving `across()` and `pick()` selections while excluding every
fixed key and grouping dimension". The copy in `R/summarize_with_margins.R`
re-derives that exclusion rule outside the owning module, so changing what a
summary selection may see is an edit in two files.

**What columns a `pick()` call selects** is written twice in one file, ~125
lines apart — `R/summary-selections.R:745` in `rewrite_pick_selection()` and
`:869` in the `"pick"` branch of `known_data_frame_output_names()`:

```r
selection <- if (length(call_args) == 0L) {
  rlang::expr(dplyr::everything())
} else {
  rlang::call2("c", !!!call_args)
}
```

`across()` has this factored out as `parse_across_arguments()`, whose header
calls itself "The one place that knows an `across()` argument can be empty, so
that no caller has to". `pick()` has no counterpart, and the two readers must
agree.

### 7. `R/factor.R:79` suppresses a lint a one-line code change removes

`margin_factor_levels()` ends in `new_levels <- if (...) ... else ...`, whose
only purpose is to be the return value, and carries
`# nolint start: object_usage_linter.` with the reason "The assignment is this
function's return value, which codetools reads as a dead store."

`AGENTS.md` *Linting* admits a `# nolint` for "a glue string or an NSE pronoun
that `codetools` cannot follow, or a name fixed by another package's API", and
says a suppression is "not a substitute for giving the linter the information it
needs". This is none of the three, and the lint is a consequence of the code
shape rather than of anything `codetools` cannot see: dropping `new_levels <-`
and returning the `if`/`else` directly is lint-clean and value-identical
(`margin_factor_levels(list(levels = c("a","b")), "T", "last")` gives
`"a" "b" "T"`, `"first"` gives `"T" "a" "b"`, both ways).

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the seven is fixed, or closed on this ticket with the evidence
      that clears it. Items 4 and 6 are the two where "recorded and not
      changed" is a plausible answer.
- [ ] Item 1's fix decides which of the two sentences is right and makes the
      other match; it does not add a third.
- [ ] Item 2's fix is verified by building a tarball from a worktree and
      confirming it holds no `.git`.
- [ ] Items 5, 6, and 7 change no behaviour: the suite passes unchanged, and
      no new test is needed for any of them.

## How they were found

The Standards axes of #40's readiness review, against `b3190d2`. Each was
reproduced independently before filing.

comments.body: Item 4 is closed without changing ADR 0010. `CONTEXT.md` supplies the current vocabulary, but `design/architecture.md` limits ADR amendments to observable decision changes. The root-row wording records the historical Parent-share decision and changing the terms would not alter that decision; new or maintained documentation will use `Grand total set`.
